//: EDICTS (docs/EDICTS.md). A law is standing and slow. An edict is a decree by whoever holds an executive position, on their own authority and without a vote: it bites at once, lasts `years` and then lapses, costs the issuer something, and in a Republic the Senate can strike it down if `annullable`. `issuer` is the position: head (the head of a house, over its own worlds), state (a consul; the chair's head while no consul sits; the Emperor), praetor, aedile (a sitting magistrate of the ladder), powers (the holder of the emergency powers, or a throne). An edict of the head falls on the house's own worlds; every other falls on the whole Reach. `cost` is paid by the issuer: influence of the year, and credits of the house in the books' hundreds. `now` is done once, the day it is proclaimed: unrest, prosperity (each world it falls on), lawlessness, allegiance (each region it falls on), manpower_per_world, credits_per_world (mustered or raised at once from each world it falls on, into the treasury of the house that holds the world), legitimacy (the issuer's house), trust (the Reach's trust in its magistrates), regard (what every other head of the Reach thinks of the issuer), requisition (manpower sent by every other house of the Reach to the issuer's), confiscate (the most, in hundreds of credits, taken from the house named: half its treasury up to that). `effects` are in force while it lasts and are the same modifier keys laws use, read by the same rules, with three of the edicts' own: debts_stayed (no instalment falls due on any loan, none is pressed, no year counts as missed), court_proof (added to the forty in a hundred at which a charge is found proved before a praetor who goes by the pleading), senate_cowed (no house but the issuer's moves a motion of its own). `opinions` is what each estate makes of it: the issuer's house is moved by that much at once. `again` is the years before it can be proclaimed again once it has ended. `outlives` true: it stands when the issuer leaves the position. `group`: only one edict of a group is in force at a time. `target` house: the edict names a house. `when` is the plain reason for which another house or magistrate proclaims it (EdictSystem.Reason).

edicts.name: An amnesty
edicts.description: Those who rose, hid or ran are forgiven and may come home. The worlds settle at once and stay quieter while it runs. The magistrates say the law has been mocked, and the officers who put the risings down are not thanked for it.
edicts.model: The Athenian amnesty of 403 BC, and Caesar's clemency after the civil war.

edicts.name: A muster of the worlds
edicts.description: Every world of the house sends men to the standards now, past what it keeps under arms in a quiet year. The fields and the yards are short of hands while it lasts, and the worlds do not like it.
edicts.model: The Roman dilectus, and the feudal summons of the ban.

edicts.name: A forced loan from the merchants
edicts.description: The merchants of the house's worlds lend what they are told to lend: four hundred credits a world, today. It is paid back at a hundred a world a year, without interest, and they do not forget who made them.
edicts.model: The Forced Loan of Charles I in 1626, and the prestiti of Venice.

edicts.name: A year's remission of the tithe
edicts.description: For one year the worlds of the house keep most of what they would have paid. The collectors stand idle, the people bless the name, and settlers come where the tithe is light.
edicts.model: The jubilee of Leviticus, and Hadrian's burning of the tax records in 118.

edicts.name: A sumptuary edict on the court
edicts.description: No silk, no plate, no feasts of more than three courses: the house and its stewards on every world keep a plain table. A hundred credits a world is saved each year and the retainers are paid less. The old blood call it a merchant's economy, and the merchants who sold the silk agree with them for once.
edicts.model: The Lex Oppia of 215 BC and the Lex Fannia of 161 BC, and the Tudor statutes of apparel.

edicts.name: A day of games
edicts.description: Races, beasts and a distribution of meat on every world of the house, at the house's cost. The worlds are quieter for it at once and for the year, and the house is thought well of.
edicts.model: The Roman ludi: bread and circuses, as Juvenal had it.

edicts.name: A corn dole
edicts.description: Grain at the state's price, or at none, on every world of the Reach. The issuer's house pays for the first of it. Every world is quieter at once and while it runs. The grain merchants are undersold and the old houses say the people are being bought.
edicts.model: The Lex Frumentaria of Gaius Gracchus in 123 BC, and the free dole of Clodius in 58 BC.

edicts.name: A requisition of men for the state
edicts.description: Every other house of the Reach sends a company to the issuer's standards now, and for two years every world musters one more than it would. No world likes to see its sons counted off.
edicts.model: The consular levy at a tumultus, when exemptions were set aside.

edicts.name: A moratorium on debts
edicts.description: While it lasts nothing falls due on any loan, to a bank, to the counting-houses or between houses. No creditor may press, no year of it counts as a payment missed, and a house that lends takes no interest. The debts are not cancelled: they wait.
edicts.model: Caesar's relief of debtors in 49 BC, and the moratoria of August 1914.

edicts.name: An edict of maximum prices
edicts.description: A highest price is set for everything the exchanges sell, a fifth under what they ask. Every house buys cheaper while it lasts. The merchants take it as theft, and say so.
edicts.model: Diocletian's Edict on Maximum Prices of 301.

edicts.name: The lanes closed to raiders
edicts.description: Patrols on every lane and every hull searched, at the issuer's cost. Lawlessness falls in every region at once and goes on falling. The searches slow the honest trade as well: a toll brings in a hundred credits less. The rim, which lives by what the patrols stop, takes it hardest.
edicts.model: The Lex Gabinia of 67 BC, which gave Pompey the sea against the pirates.

edicts.name: A day of thanksgiving
edicts.description: The temples open and the courts shut on every world, at the issuer's cost. Every region holds a little closer to the capital, the magistrates are a little better thought of, and the year is a quiet one.
edicts.model: The Roman supplicatio, decreed by the Senate and the consuls after a victory or a danger past.

edicts.name: The praetor's edict: the strict letter
edicts.description: The praetor gives notice that the court will hold a magistrate to the letter of the record. A charge is found proved fifteen times in a hundred more often, before a praetor who goes by the pleading. The Reach trusts its courts a little more. The old houses, whose sons are the ones charged, do not.
edicts.model: The praetor's edict, posted on taking office, saying how he would give judgment; and the Lex Cornelia of 67 BC that held him to it.

edicts.name: The praetor's edict: equity
edicts.description: The praetor gives notice that the court will look to what is fair and not only to what is written, and will hear what a magistrate has to say for himself. A charge is found proved fifteen times in a hundred less often. It is welcome to any house with something on the record, and it is noticed.
edicts.model: The praetor's power to give relief against the strict law: the exceptio, and restitutio in integrum.

edicts.name: The aedile's edict on the markets
edicts.description: True weights, sealed measures, and every seller to declare what is wrong with what he sells. The aedile's house pays the inspectors. Everything on the exchanges costs every house a little less while it lasts, and the Reach thinks a little better of its magistrates.
edicts.model: The edict of the curule aediles on sales in the market, which made a seller answer for hidden faults.

edicts.name: Proscriptions
edicts.description: A house is named an enemy of the state and its goods are forfeit: half of what it has, up to three thousand credits, goes to the issuer's house. Its head will not forgive it, no head in the Reach sleeps as well, and there is fear on every world while the lists are open.
edicts.model: Sulla's lists of 82 BC, and those of the Triumvirs in 43 BC.

edicts.name: Rule by decree
edicts.description: What the holder decrees has the force of law, and the chamber is told so. While it lasts no other house brings business of its own before the Senate, and a house that insists pays three influence more to move a motion. It is remembered.
edicts.model: Sulla's dictatorship for the making of laws in 82 BC, and Caesar's after him.

edicts.name: A levy in mass
edicts.description: Every exemption is set aside. Each world of the Reach sends two more to the standards of the house that holds it now, and one more a year while it lasts. There is unrest on every world for as long as it runs.
edicts.model: The levy in mass of the French Convention in August 1793.
